Read those, not all\n  of them.\n- **One check decides.** `bash .github/scripts/verify.sh` runs every check CI\n  runs, in the same order. Run it before you finish, and fix everything it\n  names. Green there is green in CI.\n- **A rule is real when something fails.** Every rule names what checks it: a\n  lint rule, the type checker, a test, the `conventions` check, or the reviewer.\n  Lint messages say how to fix; follow them.\n- **Documents over existing patterns.** Copy the code you find only where it\n  matches these documents. Where they disagree, the document wins; note the\n  difference in one line of your pull request description.\n- **These documents hold what the code cannot show.** When a reviewer flags the\n  same thing twice, it becomes a rule, with a check, in the layer it belongs to:\n  `chain/` when it holds for any project, the project's documents otherwise.\n\n---\n\n<!-- .github/conventions/chain/structure.md -->\n\n# Structure\n\nWhere this project's workspaces and features are: its architecture map,\n`docs/architecture.md`.\n\n## Feature folders\n\nCode is grouped by what it does for a user, not by what kind of file it is:\n\n```\napps/web/src/features/<feature>/     components, hooks, their tests\napps/api/src/features/<feature>/     routes, rules, data access, their tests\npackages/<shared>/src/<feature>.ts   what both sides share for that feature\n```\n\nA piece of work mostly stays inside one feature folder per workspace. Code used\nby two or more features moves to that workspace's `src/lib/`, and only then.\n\n**Why:** an issue is one behaviour end to end; when its code sits together, an\nagent finds all of it by path, and two issues in parallel rarely touch the same\nfiles.\n\n## Modules: small interface, real work behind it\n\nA module is a file or a feature folder with a few exports that do a lot. Prefer\none deeper module over several files that only pass calls through. Before adding\na file, ask what a caller would lose if it did not exist; if nothing, fold it in.\nSplit a module when it has two reasons to change, not when it grows.\n\n- One UI component per file, named after it (`TaskRow.tsx`).\n- Other files are kebab-case, named after what they do (`use-tasks.ts`).\n- Files stay under 300 lines. **Checked by** lint (`max-lines`).\n\n## Imports\n\n- **Named exports only**, so a search for a name finds every use. **Checked by**\n  lint (`import/no-default-export`; framework entry files are the exceptions,\n  and the lint config names them).\n- **No barrel files**: no `index.ts` that only re-exports. Import from the file\n  that defines the thing. **Checked by** lint. Barrels are where parallel changes\n  collide, and they hide where code lives.\n- **Between workspaces, by package name**, never by a relative path into another\n  workspace. **Checked by** lint (`import/no-relative-packages`).\n- **No import cycles.** **Checked by** lint (`import/no-cycle`).\n- **Only declared dependencies**: import a package only if the importing\n  workspace declares it. **Checked by** lint (`import/no-extraneous-dependencies`).\n\nDependencies, configuration and CI are people's work: package manifests,\nlockfiles and `.github/` cannot be changed by an agent (gh-aw protected files).\nIf a change needs a new dependency, say so in the pull request instead.\n\n## Code comes with tests, the map comes with features\n\n- A change to source files changes or adds a test that proves it. **Checked by**\n  the `conventions` check. Which test: [testing.md](testing.md).\n- A change that adds, renames, moves or removes a feature folder updates the\n  project's `docs/architecture.md` in the same pull request. **Checked by** the\n  `conventions` check.\n\n---\n\n<!-- .github/conventions/chain/testing.md -->\n\n# Testing\n\nThe project's tools for each kind of test are named in its architecture map,\n`docs/architecture.md`.\n\n## From \"Done when\" to tests\n\nAn issue's \"Done when\" is the list of tests to write: one case, one test, named\nafter the case, so a reader can tick the issue off against the test names.\n\n| The issue says | Write | Where |\n|---|---|---|\n| A table row (`Given` → `Expect`) about a rule, a route or a function | a unit or API test per row | next to the module it tests |\n| A table row about what a component shows | a component test per row | next to the component |\n| A scenario (`Given / When / Then`) | a browser test per scenario, named after its first line | the web app's `e2e/<feature>` |\n| A row or scenario of a `Component` issue (a shared component) | a story per case, named after it, whose `play` function checks it; the story is the test | next to the component |\n\n## How tests are written\n\n- **Test through the interface**: call the module, the route or the screen the\n  way its user would. Component tests find controls by role and name, as a\n  person does. A test that has to reach past the interface means the module has\n  the wrong shape.\n- **Each test starts from nothing**: a fresh database, no data or order shared\n  with another test.\n- **No network in unit and component tests**: replace the API client at its\n  seam instead of mocking the network everywhere.\n- **Time is given, not read**: code that needs \"now\" takes it as a parameter or\n  from one clock module, so tests set it. Date logic is tested at fixed times,\n  including just before and after midnight.\n- **Never weaken or delete a test to make a check pass.** If a test is wrong, say\n  why in the pull request.\n\n---\n\n<!-- docs/architecture.md -->\n\n# Tempo architecture\n\nTempo is a task app: people sign in and manage their own tasks, by list and by\nproject. The design is `design/tempo.pen`.\n\n## Workspaces\n\n| Path | Package | Holds |\n|---|---|---|\n| `apps/web/` | `@tempo/web` | The React app (Vite, TypeScript, Tailwind, React Router) |\n| `apps/api/` | `@tempo/api` | The HTTP API (Fastify, TypeScript, Drizzle over Node's `node:sqlite`) |\n| `packages/shared/` | `@tempo/shared` | The contract: Zod schemas and the types derived from them |\n\n## Features\n\n| Feature | Web | API | Shared |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| home | `apps/web/src/features/home/`: the start page, signed-in sidebar with brand and user card | `apps/api/src/features/health/`: GET /api/health | `packages/shared/src/health.ts`: HealthResponse |\n| errors | none | `apps/api/src/lib/errors.ts`: the one error shape | `packages/shared/src/errors.ts` |\n| auth | `apps/web/src/features/auth/`: sign-up, sign-in screens, sign-out hook | `apps/api/src/features/auth/`: sign-up, sign-in, GET /api/me, POST /api/auth/sign-out | `packages/shared/src/auth.ts`: sign-up, sign-in, me schemas, password rule |\n\nAdd a row when a feature folder is added, and change it when one moves or goes.\n\n## How a request flows\n\n```\nscreen (features/<f>/*.tsx)\n  → hook (features/<f>/use-*.ts)\n  → api client (src/lib/api-client.ts, parses with @tempo/shared)\n  → route (apps/api/src/features/<f>/routes.ts, validates with @tempo/shared)\n  → service (…/service.ts: the rules)\n  → repository (…/repository.ts: Drizzle, scoped to the signed-in account)\n  → SQLite\n```\n\n## Tools\n\n| Kind of test | Tool | Runs with |\n|---|---|---|\n| Unit and API tests | Vitest (API through Fastify `inject`) | `npm test` |\n| Component tests | Vitest + Testing Library (jsdom) | `npm test` |\n| Shared components | Storybook stories, each run as a test in Chromium with the accessibility check (Vitest's Storybook addon) | `npm test` |\n| Browser tests | Playwright (Chromium) against the running app | `npm test` |\n\n`bash .github/scripts/verify.sh` runs typecheck, lint, all tests and the\nconventions check. `npm run dev` starts the web app and the API together; the web\napp proxies `/api` to the API. `npm run storybook` serves the stories on\n<http://127.0.0.1:6006>.\n\nUI libraries: Radix (`radix-ui`) for interactive patterns, `class-variance-authority`\nand the `cn` helper (`apps/web/src/lib/utils.ts`) for variants, `lucide-react` for\nicons, in the shadcn/ui style (`.github/conventions/components.md`).\n\n---\n\n<!-- .github/conventions/web.md -->\n\n# Web app\n\n## Data comes through one client\n\nAll calls to the API go through `apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts`, which parses\nevery response with its schema from `@tempo/shared`. Components and hooks never\ncall `fetch` themselves. **Checked by** lint (`no-restricted-globals: fetch`\noutside the client).\n\n**Why:** one seam to replace in tests, one place where the contract is enforced,\nand a response that does not match its schema fails loudly instead of rendering\nwrong.\n\n## Components\n\n- Screens are built from the shared components (`components.md`): reuse one,\n  never rebuild it inside a feature. A part the design repeats that has no\n  shared component yet is a `Component` issue first.\n- A feature's screen state lives in a hook next to it (`use-tasks.ts`); the\n  component renders what the hook returns. Keep components free of API and\n  date logic, so the logic is tested without rendering.\n- Every screen state the design shows (loading, empty, error, disabled) is a\n  state the component can be put in, and a test puts it there.\n- Routing uses React Router: every screen is one entry in\n  `apps/web/src/routes.tsx`, and its component lives in its feature folder.\n\n## Forms\n\nValidate with the same schema the API uses (`@tempo/shared`), so the form and\nthe API refuse the same things with the same messages. Show errors where the\ndesign shows them, on the field, in the design's words.\n\n## Styling\n\n- Tailwind v4, configured in CSS: the theme is the `@theme` block in\n  `apps/web/src/index.css`. Import from the file\n  that defines the thing. **Checked by** lint. Barrels are where parallel changes\n  collide, and they hide where code lives.\n- **Between workspaces, by package name**, never by a relative path into another\n  workspace. **Checked by** lint (`import/no-relative-packages`).\n- **No import cycles.** **Checked by** lint (`import/no-cycle`).\n- **Only declared dependencies**: import a package only if the importing\n  workspace declares it. **Checked by** lint (`import/no-extraneous-dependencies`).\n\nDependencies, configuration and CI are people's work: package manifests,\nlockfiles and `.github/` cannot be changed by an agent (gh-aw protected files).\nIf a change needs a new dependency, say so in the pull request instead.\n\n## Code comes with tests, the map comes with features\n\n- A change to source files changes or adds a test that proves it. **Checked by**\n  the `conventions` check. Component tests find controls by role and name, as a\n  person does. Where they disagree, the document wins; note the\n  difference in one line of your pull request description.\n- **These documents hold what the code cannot show.** When a reviewer flags the\n  same thing twice, it becomes a rule, with a check, in the layer it belongs to:\n  `chain/` when it holds for any project, the project's documents otherwise.\n\n---\n\n<!-- .github/conventions/chain/structure.md -->\n\n# Structure\n\nWhere this project's workspaces and features are: its architecture map,\n`docs/architecture.md`.\n\n## Feature folders\n\nCode is grouped by what it does for a user, not by what kind of file it is:\n\n```\napps/web/src/features/<feature>/     components, hooks, their tests\napps/api/src/features/<feature>/     routes, rules, data access, their tests\npackages/<shared>/src/<feature>.ts   what both sides share for that feature\n```\n\nA piece of work mostly stays inside one feature folder per workspace. Code used\nby two or more features moves to that workspace's `src/lib/`, and only then.\n\n**Why:** an issue is one behaviour end to end; when its code sits together, an\nagent finds all of it by path, and two issues in parallel rarely touch the same\nfiles.\n\n## Modules: small interface, real work behind it\n\nA module is a file or a feature folder with a few exports that do a lot. Prefer\none deeper module over several files that only pass calls through. Before adding\na file, ask what a caller would lose if it did not exist; if nothing, fold it in.\nSplit a module when it has two reasons to change, not when it grows.\n\n- One UI component per file, named after it (`TaskRow.tsx`).\n- Other files are kebab-case, named after what they do (`use-tasks.ts`).\n- Files stay under 300 lines. **Checked by** lint (`max-lines`).\n\n## Imports\n\n- **Named exports only**, so a search for a name finds every use. **Checked by**\n  lint (`import/no-default-export`; framework entry files are the exceptions,\n  and the lint config names them).\n- **No barrel files**: no `index.ts` that only re-exports. Import from the file\n  that defines the thing. **Checked by** lint. Barrels are where parallel changes\n  collide, and they hide where code lives.\n- **Between workspaces, by package name**, never by a relative path into another\n  workspace. **Checked by** lint (`import/no-relative-packages`).\n- **No import cycles.** **Checked by** lint (`import/no-cycle`).\n- **Only declared dependencies**: import a package only if the importing\n  workspace declares it. **Checked by** lint (`import/no-extraneous-dependencies`).\n\nDependencies, configuration and CI are people's work: package manifests,\nlockfiles and `.github/` cannot be changed by an agent (gh-aw protected files).\nIf a change needs a new dependency, say so in the pull request instead.\n\n## Code comes with tests, the map comes with features\n\n- A change to source files changes or adds a test that proves it. **Checked by**\n  the `conventions` check. Which test: [testing.md](testing.md).\n- A change that adds, renames, moves or removes a feature folder updates the\n  project's `docs/architecture.md` in the same pull request. **Checked by** the\n  `conventions` check.\n\n---\n\n<!-- .github/conventions/chain/testing.md -->\n\n# Testing\n\nThe project's tools for each kind of test are named in its architecture map,\n`docs/architecture.md`.\n\n## From \"Done when\" to tests\n\nAn issue's \"Done when\" is the list of tests to write: one case, one test, named\nafter the case, so a reader can tick the issue off against the test names.\n\n| The issue says | Write | Where |\n|---|---|---|\n| A table row (`Given` → `Expect`) about a rule, a route or a function | a unit or API test per row | next to the module it tests |\n| A table row about what a component shows | a component test per row | next to the component |\n| A scenario (`Given / When / Then`) | a browser test per scenario, named after its first line | the web app's `e2e/<feature>` |\n| A row or scenario of a `Component` issue (a shared component) | a story per case, named after it, whose `play` function checks it; the story is the test | next to the component |\n\n## How tests are written\n\n- **Test through the interface**: call the module, the route or the screen the\n  way its user would. Component tests find controls by role and name, as a\n  person does. A test that has to reach past the interface means the module has\n  the wrong shape.\n- **Each test starts from nothing**: a fresh database, no data or order shared\n  with another test.\n- **No network in unit and component tests**: replace the API client at its\n  seam instead of mocking the network everywhere.\n- **Time is given, not read**: code that needs \"now\" takes it as a parameter or\n  from one clock module, so tests set it. Date logic is tested at fixed times,\n  including just before and after midnight.\n- **Never weaken or delete a test to make a check pass.** If a test is wrong, say\n  why in the pull request.\n\n---\n\n<!-- docs/architecture.md -->\n\n# Tempo architecture\n\nTempo is a task app: people sign in and manage their own tasks, by list and by\nproject.
